title: C482/2012/2022 of DEEPAK KUMAR Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
C-482 No. 2012 of 2022
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Amit Kapri, Advocate for the
applicant.
Mr. Atul Kumar Sah, learned
Deputy Advocate General along with Ms.
Mamta Joshi, Brief Holder for the State.
 Mr. Deep Prakash Bhatt, Advocate
for complainant-respondent no. 2.
This Court, being conscious of the
fact, that the nature of the offences,
which are subject matter of the trial of
the Special Session Trial No. 12 of 2020,
"State Vs. Deepak Kumar", where the
applicant is being tried for the offences
under Sections 323 & 376 of I.P.C., and
3/4 of the Protections of Children from
Sexual Offences, 2012, registered at
P.S. Thana Jajerdewal, District
Pithoragarh, presently pending
consideration before the court of learned
Special Judge, Pithoragarh, District
Pithoragarh, they are not compoundable
under Section 320 of the Code of
Criminal Procedure.
Today, a compounding
application being IA 2 of 2022, has been
filed by the parties.

The applicant-Deepak Kumar
and, complainant-respondent no.2,
Deeksha, are present in person, and
they have been duly identified by their
respective counsel.
This Court had even interacted
with the victim-complainant, who
submitted before the Court, that she
does not want to prosecute the present
applicant any further.
Perusal of the record reveal that
all the offences, which are complained
of against the present applicant, are not
compoundable, under Section 320 of
the Cr.P.C., but this case itself, carries a
very peculiar circumstance, where the
victim-respondent no.2, of the offence,
who is present in person before this
Court, it had been an admitted case,
that she was carrying a personal
relationship, with the present applicant,
and under a pretext of marriage, she
has voluntarily established physical
relationship, though at the age of
minority, but the peculiar facts is that
owing to the aforesaid relationship, she
conceived, and was pregnant, and later
on she had also delivered a male child
on 30.07.2019.
In the present C-482

application, which is supported with the
compounding application, the parties
have come with a case, that proceedings
of the aforesaid sessions trial, would be
a futile exercise for the reason being,
that the parties to the present C-482
application, have married each other on
25.06.2019, and as a result thereto,
both of them, are independently and
happily discharging their matrimonial
obligations, may be that it is a fact, that
the victim-respondent no.2, was minor
in the year 2018.
In view of the judgment
rendered by the Hon'ble High Court of
Punjab and Haryana, as considered by
this Court in the case of Pan Singh
Rana Vs. State of Uttarakhand
and another reported in 2018
Volume (2) U.D. 680, it provided
that, where an applicant is being tried,
even for the offences under the POCSO
Act, for establishing a physical
relationship with the female, who was a
minor, but the principles of the said
provisions have to be rationally applied,
when inevitable circumstances, comes
to the notice of the court, that because
of the physical relationship, there is a
child, which is born out of the

relationship, and the court will also
have to rationally consider the aspect,
about the solemnization of the marriage,
which was also got registered stands
fortified by the marriage notarized
agreement, which has been placed on
record with the compounding
application.
In that eventuality, in order to
maintain the family, and particularly
the interest of the male child, who has
been born out of the relationship
between the applicant and the victim-respondent no.2, the compounding
application would stand disposed off,
subject to the following conditions:
(i) That the marriage, which has
been solemnized between the
applicant and victim-respondent
no.2, on 25.06.2019, that would
be ensured to be registered by
the applicant within a period of
45 days from today.
(ii) That in an event, if the marriage
dated 25.06.2019, is not
registered by the applicant
within the aforesaid stipulated
period, the composition of the
offences, which has been made
as a consequence of today's

order, the order would be
deemed to be annulled.
Subject to the aforesaid, since it
will be absolutely a fruitless exercise to
force the present applicant, as well as,
the victim-respondent no.2, to continue
with the aforesaid special sessions trial,
owing to the peculiar circumstances,
which have arisen due to the birth of
the child, and due to solemnization of
marriage.
Accordingly, the compounding
application would stand disposed off in
terms of the conditions as mentioned
therein, which stands fortified by the
present applicant and victim-respondent no.2, as well as, which has
been fortified by the learned counsel for
the parties, who too are the signatories
to the compounding application, and
this Court having interacted with the
parties to the proceedings, both of them
admit the fact, that they are now
married, and out of the relationship,
they have a male child, and they intend
to discharge the matrimonial
obligations.
Coupled with the undertaking
given by the applicant, that he would be
taking all care and protection of the

victim-respondent no.2 in future, and
subject to the condition of registration
of the marriage solemnized on
25.06.2019, within a period of 45 days
from today, the C-482 application is
being allowed, as a consequence thereto
the proceedings of Special Session Trial
No. 12 of 2020, "State Vs. Deepak
Kumar", which is presently pending for
consideration before the court of learned
Special Judge, Pithoragarh, District
Pithoragarh, would hereby stand
dropped.
The aforesaid order, is being
passed in the peculiar circumstances of
the case, while exercising the inherent
powers under Sections 482 Cr.P.C, in
order to meet out the ends of justice,
and to balance the equities between the
parties.
